as-62 as-63 as-64 as-65 as-66 as-67 ⚙182fbad"><div class="ApiSection-MainContent ⚙ ⚙1a36ynu"><p>The Stripe API is organized around <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer"><span>REST</span></a>. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POST_(HTTP)#Use_for_submitting_web_forms"><span>form-encoded</span></a> request bodies, returns <a href="http://www.json.org/"><span>JSON-encoded</span></a> responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.</p><p>You can use the Stripe API in <a href="/sandboxes"><span>sandboxes</span></a> without affecting your live data or interacting with banking networks. The API key that you use to <a href="/api/authentication"><span>authenticate</span></a> the request determines whether the request runs in live mode or in a sandbox. Sandboxes support all v2 APIs. Test mode sandboxes support some <a href="/testing-use-cases#compare"><span>v2 APIs</span></a>.</p><p>The Stripe API doesn’t support bulk updates. You can work on only one object per request.</p><p>The Stripe API differs for every account as we release new <a href="/api/versioning"><span>versions</span></a> and tailor functionality. <a as-62 as-63 as-64 as-65 as-66 as-67 ⚙182fbad"><div class="ApiSection-MainContent ⚙ ⚙1a36ynu"><p>The Stripe API uses <a href="/keys"><span>API keys</span></a> to authenticate requests. You can view and manage your API keys in <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/login?redirect=/apikeys"><span>the Stripe Dashboard</span></a>.</p><p>Test mode secret keys start with <code class="⚙ rs-4 as-16 as-87 as-36 as-8l as-1j as-8m as-1h as-8n as-l as-26 as-8o as-8p as-27 as-28 ⚙zjuaul">sk<!-- -->_<wbr/>test<!-- -->_<wbr/></code> and have unrestricted access to their sandboxes. In live mode, you configure a <a href="/keys#create-restricted-api-key"><span>restricted API key</span></a> (starts with <code class="⚙ rs-4 as-16 as-87 as-36 as-8l as-1j as-8m as-1h as-8n as-l as-26 as-8o as-8p as-27 as-28 ⚙zjuaul">rk<!-- -->_<wbr/>live<!-- -->_<wbr/></code>) with specific API permissions. Using a restricted API key with only a subset of API permissions limits the damage a bad actor could cause if they obtained the key. In both test mode and live mode, you can create as many restricted API keys as you need for different use cases or components of your application. We also create a live mode secret key (starts with <code class="⚙ rs-4 as-16 as-87 as-36 as-8l as-1j as-8m as-1h as-8n as-l as-26 as-8o as-8p as-27 as-28 ⚙zjuaul">sk<!-- -->_<wbr/>live<!-- -->_<wbr/></code>) that grants access to all Stripe API resources. To protect your business, use restricted API keys instead.</p><p>Your API keys carry many privileges. Follow <a href="/keys-best-practices"><span>best practices</span></a> to keep your keys safe. Don’t embed secret or restricted API keys in source code or client-side applications. Instead, use your server platform’s secrets vault to provide keys to your server-side applications. If your platform doesn’t offer a secrets vault, set your keys in environment variables.</p><p>Make all API requests over <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_Secure"><span>HTTPS</span></a>. Calls made over plain HTTP fail.
